label: def:mcmkp
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:mcmkp}
Let $c$ be a positive integer.  A packing $P$ for $c$ is \emph{maximal} if $w(P)+w_j>c$ for all
$j\in I\setminus P$.  The
problem \textnormal{MinMax-Pack}\xspace asks for
$\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{P}}=\min\{v(P): P \text{ is a maximal packing for } c\}$.
head: environment
name: Maximal packing, \MCMKP

label: def:mpmkc
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:mpmkc}
Let $d$ be a positive integer.  A cover $C$ for $d$ is \emph{minimal} if
$w(C\setminus\{j\})<d$ for all $j\in C$.  The problem
\textnormal{MaxMin-Cov}\xspace asks for
$\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{C}}=\max\{v(C): C \text{ is a minimal cover for } d\}$.
head: environment
name: Minimal cover, \MPMKC

label: lem:maxchar
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Maximality is decided by the smallest excluded item

title: Proof
body_md:
No excluded item fits if and only if the lightest excluded item does not.
\ifmmode\hbox{\rlap{$\sqcap$}$\sqcup$}\else{\unskip\nobreak\hfil
\penalty50\hskip1em\null\nobreak\hfil\hbox{\rlap{$\sqcap$}$\sqcup$}
\parfillskip=0pt\finalhyphendemerits=0\endgraf}\fi
head: environment

label: lem:minchar
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:minchar}
Let $C\neq\emptyset$ be a cover for $d$.  Then $C$ is minimal if and only if
$w(C)-\min_{j\in C}w_j<d$; with integral weights,
$d\le w(C)\le d+\min_{j\in C}w_j-1$.
head: environment
name: Minimality is decided by the smallest selected item

title: Proof
body_md:
Removing the lightest selected item leaves the largest residual weight.
\ifmmode\hbox{\rlap{$\sqcap$}$\sqcup$}\else{\unskip\nobreak\hfil
\penalty50\hskip1em\null\nobreak\hfil\hbox{\rlap{$\sqcap$}$\sqcup$}
\parfillskip=0pt\finalhyphendemerits=0\endgraf}\fi
head: environment

label: cor:exactfill
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:exactfill}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),leftmargin=2em]
  \par\hangindent 40\p@ If a maximal packing $P$ for $c$ excludes an item of weight $1$,
        then $w(P)=c$.
  \par\hangindent 40\p@ If a minimal cover $C$ for $d$ contains an item of weight $1$, then
        $w(C)=d$.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment
name: Exact filling

title: Proof
body_md:
(a) is Lemma~\ref{lem:maxchar} with $\min_{j\in I\setminus P}w_j=1$.  (b) If $i\in C$
and $w_i=1$, minimality gives $w(C)-1<d$, hence $w(C)\le d$ by integrality.
\ifmmode\hbox{\rlap{$\sqcap$}$\sqcup$}\else{\unskip\nobreak\hfil
\penalty50\hskip1em\null\nobreak\hfil\hbox{\rlap{$\sqcap$}$\sqcup$}
\parfillskip=0pt\finalhyphendemerits=0\endgraf}\fi
head: environment

title: Example
body_md:
Let four items have weights $1,2,4,5$, and identify each item by its
weight.  For capacity $c=6$, both $P_1=\{2,4\}$ and $P_2=\{1,4\}$ are
maximal packings: $w(P_1)=6$, while $w(P_2)=5$ and neither excluded item
fits.  Since $w(I)=12$, the paired threshold is $d=w(I)-c=6$.
The complements $C_1=\{1,5\}$ and $C_2=\{2,5\}$ are minimal covers,
of weights $6$ and $7$, respectively.  Thus maximality and minimality
allow slack and excess, while the excluded or selected weight-$1$ item
forces exact filling in $P_1$ and $C_1$.
head: environment

label: prop:complement
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:complement}
Let $0<c<w(I)$ and $d=w(I)-c$.  A set $P\subseteq I$ is a maximal
packing for $c$ if and only if $C=I\setminus P$ is a minimal cover for $d$.
Moreover $v(C)=v(I)-v(P)$, hence $\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{C}}=v(I)-\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{P}}$ for the two paired
instances.
head: environment
name: Complementarity

title: Proof
body_md:
$w(P)\le c$ if and only if $w(C)\ge d$, and for $j\in C$,
$w(P)+w_j>c$ if and only if $w(C\setminus\{j\})<d$.
\ifmmode\hbox{\rlap{$\sqcap$}$\sqcup$}\else{\unskip\nobreak\hfil
\penalty50\hskip1em\null\nobreak\hfil\hbox{\rlap{$\sqcap$}$\sqcup$}
\parfillskip=0pt\finalhyphendemerits=0\endgraf}\fi
head: environment

label: rem:affine
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:affine}
An $\alpha$-approximation $P$ for \textnormal{MinMax-Pack}\xspace gives
$v(I\setminus P)\ge\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{C}}-(\alpha-1)\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{P}}$, an additive guarantee measured
against the wrong optimum.  Example~\ref{ex:affine} shows that no multiplicative guarantee
survives.
Approximation algorithms therefore do not transfer between the two
problems; exact algorithms and reduction gaps do.
head: environment
name: Complementation is affine, not multiplicative

label: ex:affine
title: Example
body_md:
\label{ex:affine}
Let $m\ge2$, unit costs, $m$ items of weight $1$, $m$ items of weight $m+1$,
one item of weight $m(m+1)$, and $c=m(m+1)+m$.  There are two maximal
packings: the heavy item with the $m$ unit-weight items, of cost $m+1$, and
the $2m$ other items, which weigh exactly $c$, of cost $2m$.  The latter is
a factor-$2$ approximation of $\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{P}}=m+1$, but its complement, the heavy item
alone, is a minimal cover of profit $1$, whereas $\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{C}}=m$.
head: environment

label: thm:gmp-lbp
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:gmp-lbp}
The \textnormal{\textsc{LBP}}\xspace admits a linear-time $4/3$-approximation and an FPTAS.
head: environment

label: thm:maxgreedy
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:maxgreedy}
Max Greedy sorts the items by nonincreasing weight and returns the shortest
prefix that is a cover.  If it returns $t$ items, its weight is at least
$\frac{t}{t+1}\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{C}}$; in particular it is a factor-$2$ approximation for
\textnormal{\textsc{GBP}}\xspace, and the factor is tight.
head: environment

label: thm:fls
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:fls}
\textnormal{MinMax-Pack}\xspace is weakly $\mathsf{NP}$-hard and is solved in $O(nc)$ time by dynamic
programming.  By complementarity, \textnormal{MaxMin-Cov}\xspace is weakly $\mathsf{NP}$-hard and is
solved in $O(n(w(I)-d))$ time.  The
decomposition following Lemma~\ref{lem:minchar} also solves \textnormal{MaxMin-Cov}\xspace directly
in $O(nd)$ time.
head: environment

label: thm:xu
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:xu}
Consider the problem of maximising $v(P)$ subject to
$\beta c\le w(P)\le c$, for a given $\beta\in[0,1)$.  There is an
algorithm that either reports infeasibility or returns
a feasible set of profit at least $(1-\varepsilon)$ times the optimum, in
time $O\bigl(n^2\log n/(1-\beta)+n^2/[\varepsilon(1-\beta)]\bigr)$.
head: environment

label: lem:gap
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:gap}
Let $\alpha\ge1$, and suppose a polynomial-time mapping transforms instances of
\textnormal{\textsc{Subset Sum}}\xspace to instances of an optimisation problem, together with two
numbers $g_1,g_2$ computable in polynomial time such that $g_2>\alpha\, g_1$.
If the problem is a minimisation and YES instances have $\operatorname{OPT}\le g_1$ while
NO instances have $\operatorname{OPT}\ge g_2$, or if it is a maximisation and YES
instances have $\operatorname{OPT}\ge g_2$ while NO instances have $\operatorname{OPT}\le g_1$, then
the problem admits no polynomial-time $\alpha$-approximation, unless $\mathsf{P}=\mathsf{NP}$.
head: environment
name: Gap lemma

title: Proof
body_md:
In the minimisation case an $\alpha$-approximation returns at most
$\alpha g_1<g_2$ on YES instances and at least $g_2$ on NO instances; in the
maximisation case it returns at least $g_2/\alpha>g_1$ on YES instances and
at most $g_1$ on NO instances.  Comparing the output with $g_2$, or with
$g_1$, decides \textnormal{\textsc{Subset Sum}}\xspace.
\ifmmode\hbox{\rlap{$\sqcap$}$\sqcup$}\else{\unskip\nobreak\hfil
\penalty50\hskip1em\null\nobreak\hfil\hbox{\rlap{$\sqcap$}$\sqcup$}
\parfillskip=0pt\finalhyphendemerits=0\endgraf}\fi
head: environment

label: thm:noconst
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
(a) Given $(a_1,\ldots,a_{\tilde n};b)$, let $c=b$, create an item of
weight $a_i$ and cost $0$ for each $i\in\{1,\ldots,\tilde n\}$, and a
special item $s$ with $w_s=1$ and $v_s=1$.  The instance is nontrivial since
$\sum_{i=1}^{\tilde n}a_i>b$.  If some subset sums to $b$, the
corresponding items fill the knapsack exactly and form a maximal packing of
cost $0$.  A maximal packing that excludes $s$ has weight exactly $b$ by
Corollary~\ref{cor:exactfill}(a) and consists of original items, so it
solves the \textnormal{\textsc{Subset Sum}}\xspace instance.  Hence $\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{P}}=0$ on YES instances and
$\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{P}}=1$ on NO instances.  Since $1>\alpha\cdot0$ for every $\alpha$,
Lemma~\ref{lem:gap} applies with $g_1=0$ and $g_2=1$.  On the cover side,
complementation gives $v(I)=1$, so $\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{C}}=1$ on YES instances and $\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{C}}=0$
on NO instances, and Lemma~\ref{lem:gap} applies with the same $g_1$ and
$g_2$.

(b) We may assume that $p$ has only nonnegative integer coefficients, since
increasing $p$ only strengthens the statement.  Take the same items, now
with cost $1$ for each original item and $v_s=(\tilde n+1)\,2^{p(n)}$,
where $n=\tilde n+1$.  The argument of (a) gives $\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{P}}\le\tilde n$ on YES
instances and $\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{P}}\ge v_s>2^{p(n)}\,\tilde n$ on NO instances.  On the
cover side $v(I)=\tilde n+v_s$, so $\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{C}}\ge v_s$ on YES instances and
$\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{C}}\le\tilde n$ on NO instances.  In both cases Lemma~\ref{lem:gap}
applies with $g_1=\tilde n$, $g_2=v_s$ and $\alpha=2^{p(n)}$.  The number
$v_s$ has $O(p(n)+\log\tilde n)$ bits, so the constructed instance has
polynomial size and is built in polynomial time.  As usual, running times
are measured in the binary encoding length, in which arithmetic on numbers
of polynomially many bits takes polynomial time.
\ifmmode\hbox{\rlap{$\sqcap$}$\sqcup$}\else{\unskip\nobreak\hfil
\penalty50\hskip1em\null\nobreak\hfil\hbox{\rlap{$\sqcap$}$\sqcup$}
\parfillskip=0pt\finalhyphendemerits=0\endgraf}\fi
head: environment

label: thm:unitgap
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
(a) Fix an integer $k>1/\varepsilon$, and let $m=\tilde n^k$ and $q=m+1$.  The
instance has capacity $c=qb$, an original item of weight $qa_i$ for each $i\in\{1,\ldots,\tilde n\}$,
and $m$ artificial items of weight $1$; all costs are $1$ and
$n=\tilde n+m$.  On a YES instance the original items of a solution fill the
knapsack exactly, so $\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{P}}\le\tilde n$.  On a NO instance, let $P$ be a
maximal packing that misses an artificial item, let $A$ index its original
items and $t\le m-1$ be the number of its artificial items.  By
Corollary~\ref{cor:exactfill}(a), $q\sum_{i\in A}a_i+t=qb$; reducing modulo
$q>t$ gives $t=0$ and $\sum_{i\in A}a_i=b$, a contradiction.  Hence
$\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{P}}\ge m$ on NO instances.  Since $n\le2\tilde n^k$,
\[
 n^{1-\varepsilon}\,\tilde n\ \le\ 2^{1-\varepsilon}\,\tilde n^{\,k(1-\varepsilon)+1},
\]
which is smaller than $\tilde n^k=m$ for $\tilde n$ larger than a constant
$\tilde N_\varepsilon$, because $k\varepsilon>1$; smaller instances are solved by
enumeration.  For fixed $\varepsilon$ the construction is polynomial, and
Lemma~\ref{lem:gap} with $\alpha=n^{1-\varepsilon}$ applies.

(b) Complementation keeps unit profits and gives $v(I)=n$, so $\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{C}}\ge m$ on
YES instances and $\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{C}}\le\tilde n$ on NO instances; the required
inequality $m>n^{1-\varepsilon}\tilde n$ is the one just proved.
\ifmmode\hbox{\rlap{$\sqcap$}$\sqcup$}\else{\unskip\nobreak\hfil
\penalty50\hskip1em\null\nobreak\hfil\hbox{\rlap{$\sqcap$}$\sqcup$}
\parfillskip=0pt\finalhyphendemerits=0\endgraf}\fi
head: environment

label: ex:unitgap
title: Example
body_md:
\label{ex:unitgap}
Let $a=(3,5,7)$ and $k=1$, which is smaller than the proof requires
but keeps the numbers small, so $m=3$ and $q=4$: the weights are
$12,20,28,1,1,1$.  For $b=8$ (YES), $c=32$ and $\{12,20\}$ is a maximal
packing of cost $2$.  For $b=9$ (NO), $c=36$, and a maximal packing avoiding an artificial item
would need $36=4\sigma+t$ with $t\le2$ and $\sigma$ a subset sum of
$\{3,5,7\}$; this forces $t=0$ and $\sigma=9$, which is not a subset sum.
So every maximal packing takes the three artificial items, for instance
$\{28,1,1,1\}$ of cost $4$.
head: environment

label: prop:trivial
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:trivial}
Unit-cost \textnormal{MinMax-Pack}\xspace and unit-profit \textnormal{MaxMin-Cov}\xspace admit polynomial-time
$n$-approximations: any maximal packing, found by one greedy insertion
scan, and any minimal cover, found by one greedy deletion scan, are within
factor $n$ of the optimum.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Inserting the items in any order whenever they fit gives a maximal packing,
since the residual capacity never increases; deleting items from $I$ whenever
the remainder is still a cover gives a minimal cover.  In a nontrivial
instance every maximal packing and every minimal cover is nonempty, so its
value lies between $1$ and $n$.
\ifmmode\hbox{\rlap{$\sqcap$}$\sqcup$}\else{\unskip\nobreak\hfil
\penalty50\hskip1em\null\nobreak\hfil\hbox{\rlap{$\sqcap$}$\sqcup$}
\parfillskip=0pt\finalhyphendemerits=0\endgraf}\fi
head: environment

label: cor:nofptas
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:nofptas}
Unless $\mathsf{P}=\mathsf{NP}$: (a) even on instances with integer values, neither
\textnormal{MinMax-Pack}\xspace nor \textnormal{MaxMin-Cov}\xspace admits an algorithm whose running time is polynomial in
the binary input size and $v(I)$; (b) neither unit-cost \textnormal{MinMax-Pack}\xspace
nor unit-profit \textnormal{MaxMin-Cov}\xspace admits an FPTAS.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
(a) When all item values are one, $v(I)=n$, and unit-cost \textnormal{MinMax-Pack}\xspace is $\mathsf{NP}$-hard
\citep[Theorem~7]{GaiZhang2008}; complementation keeps unit values and gives
$\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{C}}=n-\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{P}}$.  (b) The optimum is an integer in $\{1,\ldots,n\}$.  With
$\varepsilon=1/(2n)$, a scheme returns at most $(1+\varepsilon)\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{P}}<\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{P}}+1$
on the packing side and loses at most
$\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{C}}\,\varepsilon/(1+\varepsilon)<1/2$ on the cover side, so it would be
exact.
\ifmmode\hbox{\rlap{$\sqcap$}$\sqcup$}\else{\unskip\nobreak\hfil
\penalty50\hskip1em\null\nobreak\hfil\hbox{\rlap{$\sqcap$}$\sqcup$}
\parfillskip=0pt\finalhyphendemerits=0\endgraf}\fi
head: environment

label: rem:unitweights
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:unitweights}
With equal weights $w_i=w$ both problems are solved by sorting: a set is a maximal
packing if and only if it has $\lfloor c/w\rfloor$ items, and a minimal
cover if and only if it has $\lceil d/w\rceil$ items.  With weights bounded by a
polynomial in $n$ the dynamic programs are polynomial, since
$c,d\le w(I)\le n\max_{i\in I}w_i$.
However, with equal, or bounded, values
the problems remain $n^{1-\varepsilon}$-inapproximable.  Weights determine
feasibility, values only the objective; what helps on the value side is
correlation with the weights, not magnitude.
head: environment
name: Equal weights versus equal values

label: thm:nonsmall
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:nonsmall}
Fix $\delta\in(0,1]$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),leftmargin=2em]
  \par\hangindent 40\p@ If $w_i\ge\delta c$ for every item, every packing has at most
        $\lfloor1/\delta\rfloor$ items and \textnormal{MinMax-Pack}\xspace is solved exactly in
        $O(n^{\lfloor1/\delta\rfloor+1})$ time.
  \par\hangindent 40\p@ If $w_i\ge\delta d$ for every item, every minimal cover has at most
        $\lceil1/\delta\rceil$ items and \textnormal{MaxMin-Cov}\xspace is solved exactly in
        $O(n^{\lceil1/\delta\rceil+1})$ time.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
(a) A packing $P$ satisfies $|P|\,\delta c\le w(P)\le c$.  (b) A minimal
cover $C$ with lightest weight $\mu\ge\delta d$ satisfies
$(|C|-1)\mu\le w(C)-\mu<d$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:minchar}, so
$|C|-1<1/\delta$.  In
both cases enumerate the subsets of bounded size and test each in $O(n)$
time.
\ifmmode\hbox{\rlap{$\sqcap$}$\sqcup$}\else{\unskip\nobreak\hfil
\penalty50\hskip1em\null\nobreak\hfil\hbox{\rlap{$\sqcap$}$\sqcup$}
\parfillskip=0pt\finalhyphendemerits=0\endgraf}\fi
head: environment

label: prop:fptas-delta
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:fptas-delta}
Fix $\delta\in(0,1]$ and suppose $w_i-1\ge\delta(d-1)$ for every item.
Then for every $\varepsilon\in(0,1]$ a minimal cover of profit at least
$\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{C}}/(1+\varepsilon)$ can be computed in time
$O\bigl(\tfrac{n^3}{\delta}(\log n+\tfrac1\varepsilon)\bigr)$, polynomial in
$n$, $1/\varepsilon$ and $1/\delta$.  The profits are arbitrary.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
If $d=1$, every minimal cover is a singleton, so return a most profitable
item.  Hence assume $d\ge2$.
Sort the items in nondecreasing order as before
and try every item $i$ as the
first selected item of an optimal cover.
If $w_i\ge d$, the only minimal
cover with first selected item $i$ is $\{i\}$: every other selected item
has weight at least $w_i$, so any larger set $C$ would have
$w(C)-w_i\ge w_i\ge d$.  Otherwise the minimal covers with first selected
item $i$ are the sets
$\{i\}\cup C_{>i}$ with $C_{>i}\subseteq\{i+1,\ldots,n\}$ and
$d-w_i\le w(C_{>i})\le d-1$.  After discarding the items heavier than $d-1$
this is an instance of Theorem~\ref{thm:xu} with capacity $d-1$ and
$\beta_i=(d-w_i)/(d-1)$, where $1/(1-\beta_i)=(d-1)/(w_i-1)\le1/\delta$.
Run the algorithm of Theorem~\ref{thm:xu} with accuracy
$\eta=\varepsilon/(1+\varepsilon)$.  If it reports infeasibility, discard
$i$; this does not happen for the first selected item of an optimal cover.
Otherwise it returns $C_{>i}$ with $d-w_i\le w(C_{>i})\le d-1$, so
$\{i\}\cup C_{>i}$ is a minimal cover by the decomposition following
Lemma~\ref{lem:minchar}, and
$v_i+v(C_{>i})\ge v_i+(1-\eta)\operatorname{OPT}_i
\ge(1-\eta)(v_i+\operatorname{OPT}_i)=(v_i+\operatorname{OPT}_i)/(1+\varepsilon)$, where
$\operatorname{OPT}_i$ is the optimum of the residual problem.  Return the best set over
all $i$.  The second inequality uses $v_i\ge0$.  Since
$1/\eta\le2/\varepsilon$, the running time is $n$ times the
bound of Theorem~\ref{thm:xu}.
\ifmmode\hbox{\rlap{$\sqcap$}$\sqcup$}\else{\unskip\nobreak\hfil
\penalty50\hskip1em\null\nobreak\hfil\hbox{\rlap{$\sqcap$}$\sqcup$}
\parfillskip=0pt\finalhyphendemerits=0\endgraf}\fi
head: environment

label: cor:fptas-fixed-delta
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:fptas-fixed-delta}
For every fixed $\delta\in(0,1]$, \textnormal{MaxMin-Cov}\xspace restricted to instances with
$w_i-1\ge\delta(d-1)$ for all $i\in I$ admits an FPTAS.  More generally, if
$w_{\min}=\min_{i\in I}w_i\ge2$, the scheme is an FPTAS on every family of
instances on which $(d-1)/(w_{\min}-1)$ is bounded by a polynomial in the
input size.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The first statement is Proposition~\ref{prop:fptas-delta} with $1/\delta$
constant.  For the second, the proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:fptas-delta}
spends, on a candidate $i$ with $w_i<d$, time polynomial in $n$,
$1/\varepsilon$ and $(d-1)/(w_i-1)\le(d-1)/(w_{\min}-1)$.
\ifmmode\hbox{\rlap{$\sqcap$}$\sqcup$}\else{\unskip\nobreak\hfil
\penalty50\hskip1em\null\nobreak\hfil\hbox{\rlap{$\sqcap$}$\sqcup$}
\parfillskip=0pt\finalhyphendemerits=0\endgraf}\fi
head: environment

title: Example
body_md:
On $d=N$, $w=(N,N-1,N-1)$, the guess $T=\{2\}$ has $R(T)=\{3\}$, and
Max Greedy with threshold $1$ returns $\{3\}$: $\mathcal{A}_1$ records the
optimum $\{2,3\}$.
head: environment

label: lem:akfeasible
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:akfeasible}
Every set recorded by $\mathcal{A}_k$ is a minimal cover for $d$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Sets recorded in (i) are minimal covers by the test.  Let $C=T\cup G(T)$ be
recorded in (ii).  Since the guess is not discarded,
$w(G(T))\ge d-w(T)$ and $C$ is a cover.  Let $g$ be the last item added by
Max Greedy; its stopping rule gives $w(C)-w_g<d$.  Every $j\in C$ has
$w_j\ge w_g$: for $j\in T$ because $g\in R(T)$, and for $j\in G(T)$ because
Max Greedy scans by nonincreasing weight.  Hence $w(C\setminus\{j\})<d$ for
every $j\in C$.
\ifmmode\hbox{\rlap{$\sqcap$}$\sqcup$}\else{\unskip\nobreak\hfil
\penalty50\hskip1em\null\nobreak\hfil\hbox{\rlap{$\sqcap$}$\sqcup$}
\parfillskip=0pt\finalhyphendemerits=0\endgraf}\fi
head: environment

label: thm:gbpk
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:gbpk}
For every integer $k\ge0$, $\mathcal{A}_k$ returns a minimal cover $C$ with
$w(C)\ge\frac{k+1}{k+2}\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{C}}$; that is, $\mathcal{A}_k$ is a polynomial-time
$\frac{k+2}{k+1}$-approximation for \textnormal{\textsc{GBP}}\xspace.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $C^*$ be an optimal minimal cover and $z^*=w(C^*)$.  If $|C^*|\le k$,
the guess $T=C^*$ is recorded in (i).  Otherwise let $T$ consist of the $k$
heaviest items of $C^*$ and let $i^*\in C^*\setminus T$ be a lightest item
of $C^*$.  As a proper subset of a minimal cover, $T$ has $w(T)<d$; and
$C^*\setminus T\subseteq R(T)$, so $w(T)+w(R(T))\ge z^*\ge d$.  Hence
$C=T\cup G(T)$ is recorded.  The first item chosen by Max Greedy is a
heaviest item of $R(T)\ni i^*$, and the items of $T$ weigh at least
$w_{i^*}$, so $w(C)\ge(k+1)w_{i^*}$.  If $w_{i^*}\ge z^*/(k+2)$ we are done.
Otherwise Lemma~\ref{lem:minchar} applied to $C^*$ gives
$z^*<d+w_{i^*}<d+z^*/(k+2)$, that is, $\frac{k+1}{k+2}z^*<d\le w(C)$.
\ifmmode\hbox{\rlap{$\sqcap$}$\sqcup$}\else{\unskip\nobreak\hfil
\penalty50\hskip1em\null\nobreak\hfil\hbox{\rlap{$\sqcap$}$\sqcup$}
\parfillskip=0pt\finalhyphendemerits=0\endgraf}\fi
head: environment

label: cor:ptas
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:ptas}
\textnormal{\textsc{GBP}}\xspace admits a PTAS: for every fixed $\varepsilon>0$, $\mathcal{A}_k$ with
$k=\lceil1/\varepsilon\rceil-1$ is a $(1+\varepsilon)$-approximation running
in $n^{O(1/\varepsilon)}$ time.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
$k+1\ge1/\varepsilon$ gives $\frac{k+2}{k+1}\le1+\varepsilon$, and the
running time is $O(n^{k+1})$.

label: rem:gaizhang-ak
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:gaizhang-ak}
The guessing technique is the one of \citet[Theorem~3]{GaiZhang2008} for the
makespan objective of the Lazy Bureaucrat Problem with a common deadline,
and more closely of \citet[Algorithm~3 and Theorem~2]{GMP2014}, who guess
the $k$ heaviest elements of an optimal lazy matroid solution and restrict
the completion to lighter elements.  $\mathcal{A}_k$ is its cover-side
counterpart on the free matroid; the restriction to items no heavier than
the lightest guess is what keeps the output minimal
(Lemma~\ref{lem:akfeasible}).
head: environment

label: thm:gbpfptas
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:gbpfptas}
For every $\varepsilon\in(0,1]$, $\mathcal{F}_\varepsilon$ returns a minimal
cover $C$ with $w(C)\ge\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{C}}/(1+\varepsilon)$, in time $n$ times the running
time of the \textnormal{\textsc{Subset Sum}}\xspace FPTAS with accuracy $\eta$.  Hence \textnormal{\textsc{GBP}}\xspace admits an
FPTAS.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
\emph{Feasibility.}  $C^0$ is a minimal cover, and so is $\{i\}$ when
$w_i\ge d$.  A set $\{i\}\cup S_i$ is recorded only if
$d-w_i\le w(S_i)\le d-1$ with $S_i\subseteq\{i+1,\ldots,n\}$, so it is a
minimal cover by the decomposition following Lemma~\ref{lem:minchar}.

\emph{Guarantee.}  Let $C^*$ be an optimal minimal cover and $z^*=w(C^*)$.
If $z^*\le(1+\varepsilon)d$, then $w(C^0)\ge d\ge z^*/(1+\varepsilon)$.
Otherwise let $i$ be the first selected item of $C^*$.  If $w_i\ge d$, then
$C^*=\{i\}$ is recorded.  If $w_i<d$, let $S^*=C^*\setminus\{i\}$ and
$s^*=w(S^*)$, so that $d-w_i\le s^*\le d-1$; in particular $S^*$ is
feasible for the residual \textnormal{\textsc{Subset Sum}}\xspace instance.  It is optimal there:
a heavier feasible residual set would, by the decomposition following
Lemma~\ref{lem:minchar}, give a minimal cover heavier than $C^*$.
Hence $(1-\eta)s^*\le w(S_i)\le s^*$.  Since
$s^*-(d-w_i)=z^*-d>\varepsilon d$ and $\eta s^*<\eta d<\varepsilon d$, we get
$w(S_i)\ge s^*-\eta s^*>d-w_i$, so $\{i\}\cup S_i$ is recorded, and
\[
 w_i+w(S_i)\ \ge\ w_i+(1-\eta)s^*\ \ge\ (1-\eta)z^*\ =\ \frac{z^*}{1+\varepsilon}.
\]
The running time is dominated by the $n$ calls to the \textnormal{\textsc{Subset Sum}}\xspace FPTAS;
since $1/\eta\le2/\varepsilon$, it is polynomial in the input size and $1/\varepsilon$.
\ifmmode\hbox{\rlap{$\sqcap$}$\sqcup$}\else{\unskip\nobreak\hfil
\penalty50\hskip1em\null\nobreak\hfil\hbox{\rlap{$\sqcap$}$\sqcup$}
\parfillskip=0pt\finalhyphendemerits=0\endgraf}\fi

label: thm:spread
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
It suffices to consider $0<\varepsilon\le1$: for $\varepsilon>1$, running
the algorithms with accuracy $1$ gives a stronger guarantee.
(a) Let $P_\varepsilon$ be the maximal packing returned by the FPTAS of
Theorem~\ref{thm:gmp-lbp} for the objective $w$, and let $P_w^*$ and $P_v^*$
be maximal packings of minimum weight and of minimum cost.  Then
\[
 v(P_\varepsilon)\le\lambda_+w(P_\varepsilon)
 \le(1+\varepsilon)\lambda_+w(P_w^*)
 \le(1+\varepsilon)\lambda_+w(P_v^*)
 \le(1+\varepsilon)\kappa\,v(P_v^*).
\]
(b) Symmetrically, let $C_\varepsilon$ be the minimal cover returned by
the FPTAS of Theorem~\ref{thm:gbpfptas} for the objective $w$, and let $C_w^*$
and $C_v^*$ be minimal covers of maximum weight and of maximum profit.  Then
\[
 v(C_\varepsilon)\ge\lambda_-w(C_\varepsilon)
 \ge\frac{\lambda_-}{1+\varepsilon}w(C_w^*)
 \ge\frac{\lambda_-}{1+\varepsilon}w(C_v^*)
 \ge\frac{v(C_v^*)}{(1+\varepsilon)\kappa}.
\]

label: rem:linearspread
title: Remark
head: environment

title: Open problems
body_md:
The tractable cases above are sufficient conditions, not a complete
classification.
The remaining questions concern the boundary between hard and tractable instances.
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=2em,itemsep=2pt]
  \par\hangindent 40\p@ \emph{Tight approximation with unit costs or profits.}  The bounds of
        Section~\ref{sec:hard} determine the polynomial exponent but leave a
        subpolynomial gap.  Does either problem admit an
        $o(n)$-approximation, or can the lower bound be strengthened to
        $n^{1-o(1)}$?
  \par\hangindent 40\p@ \emph{Fixed spread.}  At $\kappa=1$ both problems admit FPTASs,
        whereas for unbounded $\kappa$ no factor $2^{p(n)}$ is achievable
        (Theorem~\ref{thm:noconst}(b)).
        For a fixed $\kappa>1$, is there a PTAS, or are the problems
        $\mathsf{APX}$-hard?  The neighbouring model $v_i=w_i+\text{const}$ is the
        strongly correlated class of \citet{KPP2004}.
  \par\hangindent 40\p@ \emph{Two-sided minimisation with relative slack.}  For minimising
        $v(S)$ subject to $\ell\le w(S)\le u$, even deciding feasibility is
        $\mathsf{NP}$-hard in general, since $\ell=u$ encodes \textnormal{\textsc{Subset Sum}}\xspace.  Under the
        promise $u-\ell\ge\delta u$, is there an approximation scheme
        polynomial in $1/\delta$, analogous to the scheme of \citet{Xu2013}
        for the maximisation version?  It would give the packing-side
        analogue of Proposition~\ref{prop:fptas-delta}.
  \par\hangindent 40\p@ \emph{Parameterised complexity of the no-small-items regime.}  The
        exact algorithm of Theorem~\ref{thm:nonsmall} runs in
        $n^{O(1/\delta)}$ time, hence is in $\mathsf{XP}$ for the parameter
        $1/\delta$.  Is there an $\mathsf{FPT}$ algorithm, or are the problems
        $\mathsf{W[1]}$-hard in this parameter?
\end{enumerate}
